text: After being cut, you bled, and then died.
note: was: After being cut, they bled and then died. | Player-death descriptions in this file consistently address the player as 'you' (10001, 10004, 10008); 'they' breaks that convention with no antecedent.

text: Not only were you brutally murdered, but your wealth was also completely looted.
note: was: Not only were they brutally murdered, but their wealth was also completely looted. | Player-death descriptions use 'you,' not 'they.'

text: In a martial arts duel, injuries are inevitable. text: If you die, then die, but you still made the person who stepped on you sprain their ankle. How inconsiderate of you.
note: was: If you die, then die, but you still cause others to trip and sprain their ankles. How ungrateful. | 缺德 means 'wicked/inconsiderate,' not 'ungrateful'; also tightens to the one person who stepped on you, matching the singular implication of the source.

text: You should have behaved yourself when you had the chance.
note: was: Usually, I just want you to be a good person. | 平時就讓你好好做人了 is a retrospective rebuke ('[I] already told you to behave'), not a present-tense wish; matches the death-caption's too-late-now tone.

text: You were thrown into the furnace and refined alive. The pill made from you was thrown into the river to feed the fish.
note: was: You were thrown into the furnace, burned alive. The elixir made from you was thrown into the river to feed the fish. | 煉 is alchemical refining (matches the 丹藥 made from you), not simply 'burned'; NOMENCLATURE explicitly lists 'Elixir' as an avoid form for 丹 - 'Pill' is the fixed term.

text: You Tang Clan traitor - you deserve to die.
note: was: You traitor of the Tang Clan, you deserve to die. | Smoother phrasing of the direct address, same meaning, ASCII hyphen.

text: Your martial arts skills are truly lacking. Eldest Senior Brother thought you could handle it, but in the end, it was too late to even try to save you.

text: Ambushed and assassinated by a female thief.
note: was: Ambushed and assassinated by a Female Bandit | Same nomenclature fix as the title; sentence case with terminal period for a description row.

note: was: Your enemy from Kongtong has finally met their just end, having committed countless evils and perished by execution. | The source addresses the player directly (你這崅峽之敵, 'you, this enemy of Kongtong'); the old text wrongly turned it into a third party ('your enemy'), so no one actually dies in the old sentence - a serious subject error for a record of the player's own death.

text: The vulgar villain wanted to show their power, often casually killing a few passersby to demonstrate their ruthlessness. And so, you were killed.
note: was: The vulgar villain wanted to show their power, often casually killing a few passerby to demonstrate their ruthlessness. And so, you were killed. | 'passerby' is singular; the correct plural is 'passersby.'

text: The doctor advised you to rest seriously; it wasn't a joke. You insisted on creating your own excuses and moving around, and now look what happened: you'll never have to move again.

text: On this day, the Tang Clan's rebels were wiped out entirely at Meishan; not one survived. The Outer Fort was burned to the ground, and all merit and blame turned to nothing. You once lived, only no one remembers it anymore.
note: was: On this day, the rebels of the Tang Clan were completely annihilated at Meishan, with not a single one surviving. The fortress outside the courtyard was set ablaze, and all achievements and failures have turned to nothing. You have survived, but no one remembers you. | 'You have survived' directly contradicts 'not a single one surviving' just stated - 你們活過 means they once lived, not that they

text: You are alive, yet you have been dead for a long time.\nXiahou Lan regrets that she bound you that day, making you suffer decades more than you should have.
note: was: You are alive, yet you have been dead for a long time. Xiahou Lan regrets that day when they bound you, making you suffer for several more decades. | Xiahou Lan is established as female in the register (her sobriquet's 蘭 echoes her real name); fixed 'they' to 'she,' and restored the dropped \n.

text: When a person dies, it is like a lamp going out - you burned through the last of your life's fire and paid your enemies back in kind.\nDecades later, the world still remembers that peerless final stand of the Tang Clan.
note: was: When a person dies, it's like a lamp extinguished; you have burned out the fire of life, yet still, you leave behind colors. Decades later, the world will still remember the Tang Clan's exquisite echoes. | 還以顏色 is the idiom 'to give someone a taste of their own medicine,' not literally 'to leave behind colors'; also restored the dropped \n.

text: There is no longer a Tang Clan in this world, but its flame has never gone out. There is you, and Junior Martial Sister, and the family you will yet have together.\nThe Tang Clan began as one family, and in the end, it remains one family. The Tang family's flame will carry on.
note: was: There is no longer a Tang Clan in this world, but the flame has not been extinguished. With you, Junior Martial Sister, and your future family, the Tang Clan was originally one family, and in the end, it remains one family. The legacy of the Tang family will continue to be passed down. | 'With you...the Tang Clan was originally one family' did not connect grammatically; restructured, and rest

text: Your journey never stopped from the day you set out, playing your way wherever you went - she paid for it, you risked your life for it. You visited old friends without holding back, roamed the length of the Divine Land, and your footsteps finally came to rest at Mount Kunlun.
note: was: Your journey has not stopped since the day you set off, playing wherever you go. They pay for everything while you give your all, visiting old friends without holding back your feelings, traveling all over the land, with your footsteps finally resting at Kunlun Mountain. | 她 marks a specific 'she,' not 'they'; also 你賣命 is closer to 'you risked your life' than the vaguer 'you give your all'; '

text: Thanks to Shangguan Ying, the Zhao family became one of the wealthiest households in the region.\nShangguan Ying gradually handed the business over to you, while she took charge of running the household.\nAs a virtuous wife and mother, she never struck the children; if they misbehaved, she struck you instead.
note: was: Thanks to Shangguan Ying, the Zhao family became one of the wealthiest households in the region. Shangguan Ying gradually handed over the business to you, while she took charge of the household affairs. As a virtuous wife and mother, she never hit the children; if the children made a mistake, she would discipline you instead. | Restored the two dropped \n's.

text: Xiaomei is usually wise and gentle, but when provoked, she can become fierce and overpowering. She once wielded a blade to threaten every woman within a hundred-mile radius, warning them to stay away from you.
note: was: Xiao Mei is usually wise and gentle, but when provoked, she can become fierce and overpowering. She once wielded a blade to intimidate all the women within a hundred‑mile radius, warning them not to come near you. | Matches the name fix above, and fixes the patch's U+2011 hyphen in 'hundred‑mile.'

text: You and Xiaozhu built an exquisitely intricate automaton and hid it beneath the water of a pond. Because its mechanism was too complex, it had to be built larger, split into a man, a lion, and an eagle that could combine into one.\nSuch an achievement was enough to earn a place in history, but for fear the automaton might be put to evil use, you ultimately chose to destroy it.
note: was: You and Xiao Zhu created an exquisitely intricate automaton, hidden beneath the water of the pond. Due to the complexity of its mechanisms, it had to be made larger, divided into a human, a lion, and an eagle, which could combine into one. Such an achievement was enough to be remembered in history, but fearing that the automaton might be misused, you ultimately decided to destroy it. | Restor

note: was: You and your spouse possess noble character without arrogance. Scholars and refined individuals, as well as merchants and common folk, all welcome you without reservation. You engage in conversation with learned scholars and do not refuse the company of ordinary people; you can be friends with everyone from scholars to farmers and merchants, treating each person with equality, respect, and si

text: Long Yuan came quietly to see you both. For a moment his eyes blazed with fury, but thinking of his own lack of accomplishment, he decided to just let you be.\nAfter all, whether lived gloriously or lived quietly, it is still a life either way. Your father-in-law doesn't ask much of you - he doesn't need you to look after the world, just to protect your own family. Being her hero is enough.
note: was: Long Yuan quietly came to see you all, and for a moment, they were so angry that their vision blurred. Thinking about their own lack of accomplishments, they decided to let you be. After all, living a grand life or passing through peacefully is still a life. Your father‑in‑law does not ask much of you; you don't need to care for the world's people, just protect your own family. Being her hero

text: Sometimes you don't even need a script; you can make people laugh just by talking off the cuff. The stranger you look, the more popular you become - which is how you learn that crosstalk is your true calling. In this field, you're even more popular than Eldest Senior Brother, with a talent he can only envy and never match.
note: was: Sometimes you don't even need to prepare a script; just speaking off the cuff can make people laugh. The stranger you look, the more popular you become, which makes it clear that cross‑talk is your calling. In this field, you are even more popular than Senior Brother, possessing talents that they can't help but envy. | 大師兄 is the register's 'Eldest Senior Brother,' not the bare 'Senior Brothe

text: Gengyang Reading Studio will compile your deeds into a book and publish it in the market.\nThe name of the Tang Clan's Living Hero will spread across the Central Plains overnight, known to every last person.\nFrom now on, your name will be legend, revered by thousands.
note: was: Gengyang Reading Studio will compile your deeds into a book and publish it in the market. The renowned reputation of the Tang Clan's chivalrous hero will soon spread throughout the Central Plains, known by all and acknowledged by everyone. text: You became an Emei Disciple, enjoying the same treatment and duties as everyone else.\nAs a member of the Wulin, you took part in a few major events of the martial world, neither gaining great merit nor incurring blame, and retired into seclusion in your old age.
note: was: You became an Emei Disciple, enjoying the same treatment and obligations as others. As a member of the Wulin, you participated in several significant events, neither achieving great merit nor incurring blame, and eventually retired in seclusion when you grew old. | Restored the dropped \n.

text: Beaten down by random blows from this heartless world, your heart died long before your body ever did.
note: was: In this ruthless world, being struck by chaotic fists, your heart has a shorter lifespan than your body; it has long since died. | The original was an awkward run-on; tightened into one clear clause.

text: Your backbone vanished the instant your actual bones broke.
note: was: Your spirit vanished the moment your bones were broken. | 骨氣 (backbone/integrity) puns on 骨頭 (bones) in the source; 'backbone' keeps that wordplay, which 'spirit' loses.

text: No one kept you there, yet you could not bear to leave. For the rest of your life, you stayed trapped before her grave, weeping in repentance - but how could she ever answer?
note: was: No one has kept you, yet you are reluctant to walk away. Throughout your life, you remain trapped before her grave, shedding tears of remorse, but how could she ever respond? | Past-tense narration for consistency with the rest of the entry.

text: No matter how many times I am reborn, I am willing to cross the River Styx and pass through hell for her.
note: was: No matter how many times I reincarnate, I am willing to traverse the River of Oblivion and cross through hell for her. | 冥 means 'the underworld,' not 'oblivion' (forgetting); 'River Styx' is the genre-appropriate underworld river.

text: From this moment on, you are a changed person - just as you once looked up to Eldest Senior Brother, your junior brothers and sisters now trust you too.
note: was: From this moment on, you will be reborn, just as you once looked up to Senior Brother; your junior brothers and sisters will also trust you. | 大師兄 is the register's 'Eldest Senior Brother,' not the bare 'Senior Brother.'

text: Who doesn't want to be favored by fate, to turn the world upside down, and return home to a harem? But you still have to stay alive and remain clear-headed.
note: was: Who doesn't want to be favored by fate, to turn the world upside down, and return home to a harem? But you still have to stay alive and remain clear‑headed. | Fixed the patch's U+2011 hyphen to an ASCII hyphen.

text: The wounds left on you by the Wulin Alliance Leader and the Thousand Faced Demon are marks of your honor.
note: was: The wound left by the Leader of the Wulin Alliance and the Thousand Faced Demon is a mark of your honor. | The register's fixed English for 武林盟主 is 'Wulin Alliance Leader,' not 'Leader of the Wulin Alliance.'
was: I am not going anywhere | Descriptions are sentences and take terminal punctuation.

was: The companion of the sect leader | 兼 ('concurrently/also') marks this as a secondary title, which the patch dropped; also capitalizes 'Sect Leader' per the register and adds the terminal period descriptions take.

text: Traveling far and wide, living by chivalry and justice, she has fallen completely for your heroic spirit.
note: was: Traveling far and wide, acting with chivalry, they have fallen in love with your heroic spirit. | 她 marks a specific 'she,' not 'they'; also renders the full idiom 行俠仗義 ('chivalry and justice') instead of dropping its 仗義 half.

text: He has his own opportunities, but without you, the Flying Hero's return would have been delayed indefinitely.
note: was: They have their own opportunities, but without you, the return of the Flying Hero will be indefinitely delayed. | 他 refers to the (male) Flying Hero, not a generic 'they.'

text: You and Junior Martial Sister are married, and the two of you travel together. It is said that the daughters of the Tang Clan are cold as ice and rarely smile, yet travelers who see her by your side find that she always wears a bright smile.
note: was: You and Junior Martial Sister have become a couple and are traveling together. It is said that the daughters of the Tang Clan are as cold as ice and rarely smile, yet passersby see her by your side and always wear bright smiles. | Verified against the live row (line 382) and the quoted old text matches exactly. 結為夫妻 is a wedding, not merely 'a couple becoming a thing' - the old wording unders

With you indulging and pampering her, she fears nothing; her mischief never quiets down, even into old age, yet this life is complete and she has no regrets. In this era of strict moral codes, with no parents' command and no matchmaker's word, they stay together purely because they suit each other.
note: was: Yunshang and you hold hands to wander through Jiangnan, taking a boat to listen to the rain and sleep. With you by their side, cherished and adored, they are fearless, their past filled with misdeeds, never settling down until old age, living this life without regrets. text: I Detest the World, Just as the World Detests Me
note: was: I detest the world, just as the world detests me. | Title Case, no trailing period, per house style for Records titles (GLOSSARY line 8).

was: Pili Jiao Frog | 屁力焦蛙 is a joke technique name built from meaningful characters (fart-power / scorched / frog); NOMENCLATURE rule 2 requires such names be translated as a noun phrase, never left as pinyin like 'Pili Jiao Frog.' The crude literal rendering matches the source's lowbrow joke register.

text: I Am at the Bottom of the Tang Clan Valley
note: was: I am at the bottom of the Tang Clan valley. | Title Case, no period; Tang Clan matches NOMENCLATURE.
was: Stabbed by Xiao Mei | NOMENCLATURE fixes the short form as one word, 'Xiaomei.'

was: Jianghu Vendetta Order: Kongtong | House style uses ' · ' (U+00B7) as the name/subtitle separator (GLOSSARY, and NOMENCLATURE's own worked example 'Kongtong Sect · Flying Heaven Gate'), not a colon.
was: Like the Dark Sorcerer | The paired description explains the epithet as both 'darkness' and 'Grand Sorcerer' combined; the old title dropped 'Grand,' contradicting its own explanation.

text: The Loneliest Thing in the World Is Parting from You
note: was: The world is desolate, especially when I am apart from you. | 寂寥事 names parting from her as the loneliest thing in the world, not a general claim about the world; Title Case, no trailing period.

text: The Loneliest Thing in the World Is Parting from You
note: was: The world is desolate, especially when I am apart from you. | Identical source text to Library/Title/20013 must render identically.

text: Apes and Cranes, Insects and Sand
note: was: Yuanhe Chongsha | A meaningful classical allusion (explained in full in the description) should be translated, not left as untranslated pinyin.

text: Enter the Gate of Infinity, Roam the Boundless Fields
note: was: Enter the gate of infinity, roam the boundless fields. | Title Case, no trailing period.

text: The End of Grace and Vengeance
note: was: The End of Grudges and Affections | 恩 here is a debt of kindness/gratitude repaid, not romantic 'affection'; matches the description's 'repaid both kindness and vengeance.'
was: The Hidden Weapons of the Tang Clan | The register's fixed English for 唐門暗器 is 'Tang Clan Hidden Weapons'; use it verbatim rather than a paraphrase.
was: Xiao Mei's Secret Collection | The register fixes the short form of 虞小梅 as one word, 'Xiaomei,' not 'Xiao Mei.'

text: What You Wish For, Let It Be a Journey Through Jianghu
note: was: What you wish for, let it be a journey through Jianghu. | Title Case, no trailing period.
was: Annoying Cultivation | The register's fixed compound for 修仙 is 'Immortal Cultivation,' not bare 'Cultivation' (reserved for the 修養 stat).
was: Carefree Heroes | 侶 specifically means a couple/pair, which plain 'Heroes' loses; the description confirms a romantic pairing.
was: Fujian Province | NOMENCLATURE explicitly says to drop 'Province' unless the source has 省, which this row does not; 'Fujian Province' is the avoid-term.

text: Go to the dark and dim Alchemy Room to be at someone's disposal.
note: was: Go to the dark and dim alchemy room to be at someone's disposal. | Matches the established place name Alchemy Room (Position/Name/Alchemy) elsewhere in this file.

text: Although the Alchemy Room is the most important, since the Second Senior Brother is at home, there's no need for others to interfere, is there?
note: was: Although the alchemy room is the most important, since the Second Senior Brother is at home, there's no need for others to interfere, is there? | Matches the established place name Alchemy Room.

text: The fire in the alchemy room, burning steadily for years without fail, will finally go out today.
note: was: The fire in the alchemy room, which has burned for years without dying, is finally going to go out today, oh. | The trailing 'oh' literally renders the sentence-final particle 啊, reading as an unintended interjection in English.

text: Prepare enough firewood and daily water for the whole Tang Clan for tomorrow. No one wants this exhausting chore. Plus, the path is steep - you have to watch every step to avoid a deadly fall. Then again, making a few more trips might improve your Qinggong, heh.
note: was: Prepare enough firewood and daily water for the Tang Clan for tomorrow. No one wants to do this arduous task, as it's exhausting. In addition, the path is steep, so one must take each step carefully to avoid falling to death. Running multiple trips might inadvertently improve their light steps, heh. | NOMENCLATURE: 輕功 is Qinggong, never 'light steps'; also fixes the pronoun shift and tightens

text: Go to the back mountain to pay respects to the Eldest Senior Brother.
note: was: Go to the back mountain to pay respects to Master Brother. | NOMENCLATURE/GLOSSARY: 大師兄 is Eldest Senior Brother; Master Brother is the explicitly flagged wrong, patch-only rendering.

text: Since the hidden weapons used for practice are loaded with ink, no matter how thoroughly you sweep, the place is bound to be a mess again after each morning's exercises. Someone has to keep it tidy.
note: was: Due to the fact that the practice hidden weapons are loaded with ink, no matter how clean you sweep, after daily morning exercises, it will definitely become very messy. Someone has to tidy up the environment. | Trims the wordy 'due to the fact that' filler.

text: Training Ground... does it need someone guarding it? Where should I hide? Behind the pillar?
note: was: Training ground... do we need someone to guard it? Where should I hide? Behind the pillar? | Capitalizes 'Training Ground' as the place name, matching the register's Training Ground place-name convention (same location as Position/Name/Center).

text: Head down the mountain to purchase daily necessities. It's good to get some fresh air, but often, once you go, you can't come back for days.
note: was: Head down to the mountain to purchase daily necessities. It's good to get some fresh air, but often, once you go, you can't come back for days. | 'Down to the mountain' reverses/obscures the intended direction of 下山 (descending from the mountain).

text: Or perhaps I should just stay out of this mess; I can tell there's no reward. Whether I'm there or not, the Tang Clan doesn't care. If things go wrong, I might even lose my life, and no one would even mourn me. ...Perhaps I should just carry a lantern and go down the mountain.
note: was: Or perhaps I should just stay out of this mess; I can tell there's no reward. Whether I'm there or not, the Tang Clan doesn't care. If I do something wrong, I might even lose my life, and no one would mourn. ...Perhaps I should just carry a lantern and go down the mountain. | 一個不好 means 'if things go badly' (bad luck), not 'if I do something wrong' (personal fault).

text: Go to that scorching Forge to be at someone's disposal.
note: was: Go to that scorching forge to be at someone's disposal. | Matches the established place name Forge, consistent with the Alchemy Room/Kitchen/Training Ground fixes elsewhere in this file.

text: There are many mechanisms and hidden weapons in the Forge, so it's not strange that bandits would covet them.
note: was: There are many mechanisms and hidden weapons in the forge, so it's not strange that bandits would covet them. | Matches the established place name Forge.
was: No longer need to knock and beat | Restores the missing period and reads more naturally than the literal 'knock and beat' for onomatopoeic 敲敲打打.

text: To avoid being discovered, I had to hide on the cliff outside the Women's Quarters starting in broad daylight, keeping watch and waiting patiently for my chance. When night fell, the Junior Martial Sister would fold paper cranes by the window. I didn't intend to do anything wrong - I just wanted to listen to her breathing!
note: was: To avoid being discovered, I had to hide outside the female disciple's room on the cliff edge during the day, waiting like a rabbit in a trap. When night fell, the junior martial sister would fold paper cranes by the window. I didn't intend to do anything wrong; I just wanted to listen to her breathing! | Fixes nomenclature (Women's Quarters, Junior Martial Sister) and corrects 守株待兔, which de

text: If it weren't broad daylight, the moment I got near the Women's Quarters, the sisters would surround me and beat me senseless without a word of warning.
note: was: If it's not daylight, I would be surrounded and beaten up by the sisters without hesitation as soon as I approach the female disciple's room. | Nomenclature fix (Women's Quarters) and clearer cause-then-effect reading.

text: Is it really my place to worry about the Women's Quarters?
note: was: Is the female disciple Fang Lun worried about me coming? | 輪得到 is a set phrase for 'is it even my place/turn to...', not a person's name - the patch mis-parsed it as a character called 'Fang Lun'. Also fixes 女弟子房 to Women's Quarters.

text: The sisters of the sect are leaving this place, and who knows where they'll find shelter in the days ahead.
note: was: The sisters of the sect are leaving this place; in the future, they do not know where to take shelter. | Fixes the tense mismatch and renders the impersonal 不知 idiomatically.

text: If Fourth Senior Brother is present, he would definitely guard the Kitchen. Why would bandits launch a surprise attack on the Kitchen? To destroy our stored grain?
note: was: If Fourth Senior Brother is present, he would definitely guard the mess hall. Why would bandits launch a surprise attack on the mess hall? To destroy our stored grain? | 伙房 = Kitchen, already fixed for this exact location in this file; 'mess hall' is an unregistered term.

text: The Tang Clan's food was never any more fragrant than an ordinary household's, but I'll surely miss it after this.
note: was: The Tang Clan's food didn't smell as fragrant as that of ordinary households, but in the future, they couldn't help but miss it. | Fixes the pronoun shift ('they') that breaks the first-person voice used throughout this scene.

text: Hurry up and get to the training ground for morning exercises.
note: was: Hurry up and go to the school yard for morning exercises. | 校場 is a martial drill/training ground, not a children's 'school yard'.

text: Afraid that if someone tried to talk me into staying, I might waver, so I left without a word.
note: was: In case they were comforted by others, it might cause hesitation, so they left without saying goodbye. | 慰留 means 'persuade someone to stay', not 'comfort'; restores the first-person voice used elsewhere in this scene.

text: Let's prepare to depart for Kui Prefecture.
note: was: Let's prepare to depart for Kui Prefecture | Restores the missing final period.

text: Go find the Second Senior Brother.
note: was: Go find the Second Senior Brother | Restores the missing final period.

text: Hurry up and go to the Alchemy Room!
note: was: Hurry up and go to the alchemy room! | Matches the established place name Alchemy Room.

text: Go to Zhengxin Hall for the meeting - the Third Senior Brother is waiting for me.
note: was: Go to Zhengxin Hall for the meeting, Third Senior Brother is waiting for me. | Fixes the comma splice.

text: Third Senior Brother needs to bathe, burn incense, fast, and observe a three-day abstinence to offer prayers to the ancestors of the Tang family. I'll go do something else first.
note: was: Third Senior Brother needs to bathe, burn incense, fast, and observe a three‑day abstinence to offer prayers to the ancestors of the Tang family. I'll go do something else first. | Strips the non-ASCII U+2011 hyphen.

text: Serving as a day attendant at Zhengxin Hall involves only simple and refined tasks. Not only does it not cause mental strain, but it also aids in self-cultivation. However, always choosing such light work might draw envy.
note: was: Serving as a day attendant at Zhengxin Hall involves only simple and refined tasks. Not only does it not cause mental strain, but it also aids in self‑cultivation. However, always choosing such light work might draw envy. | Strips the non-ASCII U+2011 hyphen.

text: Zhengxin Hall is guarded by the Sect Leader; even the wildest bandits wouldn't be reckless enough to throw their lives away there, would they? Would it be too pretentious of me to go guard Zhengxin Hall?
note: was: Zhengxin Hall is guarded by the master; even if the bandits are as reckless as they can be, they wouldn't go to their death, would they? Would it be too pretentious for me to guard Zhengxin Hall? | GLOSSARY explicitly warns against 'Master' for 掌門; the correct title is Sect Leader.

text: Go and prostrate yourself before the Sect Leader, and put out the lights of Zhengxin Hall.
note: was: Go and prostrate yourself before the sect leader, and put out the lights of Zhengxin Hall. | NOMENCLATURE capitalizes 掌門 as the title Sect Leader.

text: I'd better not go in and ask for trouble - Senior Brother has no intention of letting me get a word in. He says the same thing every time, and his fist comes swinging before I even finish.
note: was: I'd better not go in to challenge him; Senior Brother had no intention of letting me speak. He was saying the same words, and his fist swung over. | 'His fist swung over' is an awkward literal phrasing; tightened for a natural habitual-tense reading.

text: In the past, I always complained the dormitory was too crowded; now it won't be nearly as lively.
note: was: In the past, I always found the common place too crowded, but later it wasn't as lively anymore. | 通舖 is a shared dormitory bunk, not 'the common place' (which the old text mis-parsed as a place name).

text: I'm the Third Senior Brother's assistant, helping to handle all the sect's miscellaneous affairs, and doubling as librarian for the Scripture Hall's collection, keeping track of lending records. In my spare time, I get to browse the books myself, which is rather nice.
note: was: Serving as the assistant to the Third Senior Brother, helping to handle all the miscellaneous affairs of the sect. Also serving as the librarian for the lecture hall's collection, specializing in lending records. In their spare time, they can also browse through books themselves, which is quite nice. | Names the location by its register name (Scripture Hall, matching Position/Name/Study = 講經堂

text: The Scripture Hall once suffered a calamity by fire, and holds few martial arts manuscripts these days, but it's still a key location of the Tang Clan. The Third Senior Brother is surely among those guarding it.
note: was: The Lecturing Hall once suffered a calamity of the fire god, with few martial arts manuscripts, but it is still a key location of the Tang Clan. One might think that the Third Senior Brother must be among those guarding it. | Uses the register's place name (Scripture Hall, from Position/Name/Study) instead of the inconsistent 'Lecturing Hall' for what is the same building.

text: The Tang Clan's history really ought to be written down, so it can be passed on for posterity.
note: was: Regarding the Tang Clan's affairs, they should be written down and passed down for the good. | 'Passed down for the good' is not idiomatic English.
was: Pharmacy | GLOSSARY/NOMENCLATURE: this shop = Apothecary, avoid 'Pharmacy'; confirmed by the paired Position/desc/doctor row which already renders the same shop as 'apothecary'.
was: Shangqing Temple | NOMENCLATURE's suffix table maps 宮 to Palace; no override entry exists for this landmark, so the suffix rule governs.

text: Developing poisons to carry on the sect's arts, and compounding everyday remedies to sell down the mountain - all to make a living.

text: Make a living by fighting on the duel platform.
note: was: Make a living by fighting on the fighting platform. | Removes the duplicated 'fighting...fighting platform' and matches the Duel Platform label.

text: Not many people strike it rich - far more lose everything. Yet the naive marks keep lining up all the same.
note: was: Not many people achieve wealth and success; instead, many lose everything. Yet the naive sheep still follow one after another. | 羊牯 is gambling slang for a mark/sucker, not literally sheep; literal rendering reads oddly in English.

text: Preparing dishes in the kitchen - usually no one will fight you for the wok and spatula - and the menu is entirely up to your whim.
note: was: Preparing dishes in the kitchen, usually no one will try to take the wok and spatula from you, the menu entirely depends on your whim. | Fixes the comma-spliced run-on.

text: True Cultivators should receive the Zhengyi register, practice the Heavenly Heart Righteous Law, and eliminate the false to preserve the true.
note: was: True Cultivators should receive the Zhengyi register, practice the Heavenly Heart Righteous Law, and eliminate falsehoods to preserve the true. | 去偽存真 is a fixed parallel idiom (discard the false, retain the true); 'the false' restores the needed parallel to 'the true'.

text: Cover for the perpetually late Tang Fang as the doctor on duty for a while - the consultation fees are yours to keep.
note: was: Help Tang Fang be a sitting‑in doctor for a while; the consultation fee is yours. | Fixes the non-ASCII hyphen and clarifies the substitution sense of 慣性遲到 (habitually late); Tang Fang's name kept per the register.

text: Working under the blazing sun at the Righteous Field teaches you the hardships of common life, and leaves the heart steadier and more grounded.
note: was: Under the great sun, going to the Righteous Field to cultivate teaches one about the hardships of life, making the heart become more steady and grounded. | Fixes the clumsy gerund-headed opener; 義田 = Righteous Field kept intact, meaning preserved.

text: Forge iron tools, produce essential household items, and sell them to sustain the sect's livelihood.
note: was: Forge iron tools, produce essential household items, and sell them to sustain the family's livelihood. | 師門 means 'the sect', not 'the family'.

text: At Kongtong's great ironworks, they forge tools and produce daily necessities, then sell them for a profit.
note: was: In Kongtong's large iron forge, they forge ironware, produce daily necessities, and sell them to make a profit. | Removes the redundant 'forge...forge ironware'.

text: This isn't your home; you have to pay to borrow a hammer from the smithy.
note: was: This isn't your home; you have to pay to borrow a hammer from the iron shop. | 'Iron shop' implies a retail store; sibling desc (forge2) calls the same kind of place a forge, so 'smithy' fits a place where a hammer is borrowed for work.

text: All who join my Flying Heaven Gate seek to become immortals - sitting in meditation, practicing the Kongtong Immortal Arts, striving to ascend to the heavens in broad daylight, transcending the Three Realms and beyond the Five Elements.
note: was: Enter my Flying Heaven Gate, all are seekers of immortality. Meditate and practice Kongtong Immortal Arts, seeking to ascend to heaven by day, breaking through the three realms, beyond the five elements. | Fixes the comma-spliced opener and clarifies 白日飛昇 (ascending while alive, in daylight); no placeholder/\n was present to lose (the old row already lacked one).

text: Burning incense and brewing tea - the easy work of attending study sessions and waiting on your elders. Constant exposure may rub off a touch of refinement, but it hardly counts as an accomplishment.
note: was: Burning incense and brewing tea, the relaxed task of accompanying reading and serving the master. Gradually influenced by hearing and seeing, one can absorb a bit of refined atmosphere, but it doesn't count as much of a merit. | Fixes the dangling gerund opener and the uncountable misuse of 'merit'.

text: In the past, the Junior Martial Sister loved folding paper cranes too - now the scene remains, but she is gone. You can no longer see her face; only folding paper cranes can offer you comfort.
note: was: In the past, the junior martial sister also loved folding paper cranes. Now, things are different. You can't see her face; only folding paper cranes can console you. | Capitalizes the register title and restores the 'the setting remains, the person is gone' sense of 物是人非 that 'things are different' flattens.

text: The Oath of Zhengyi Mengwei: A Daoist priest should take it as their duty to subdue demons and eliminate evil spirits!
note: was: The Oath of Zhengyi Mengwei: A Taoist priest should take it as their duty to subdue demons and eliminate evil spirits! | NOMENCLATURE is explicit: use Dao- spellings, never Tao-.

text: Go to the back mountain to cut firewood and carry it back to the sect for use. Not only is it arduous, but the mountain path has been neglected for years, and every time one walks it, it's a heart-pounding experience.
note: was: Go to the back mountain to cut firewood and carry it back to the sect for use. Not only is it arduous, but the mountain path has been neglected for years, and every time one walks it, it's a heart‑pounding experience. | Strips the non-ASCII U+2011 hyphen.

text: Participate in group training, strengthen your physique, pour out youthful sweat, and build camaraderie with your fellow disciples.
note: was: Participate in group training, strengthen your physique, spill the sweat of youth, and enhance camaraderie among fellow disciples. | 'Spill the sweat of youth' is an overly literal rendering of 揮灑汗水青春; the fix reads more naturally in English.

text: Rest is meant to help you go further. But moderate rest is called taking a break, while rest without restraint is called laziness.
note: was: Rest is to go further. However, moderate rest is called taking a break, and uncontrolled rest is called laziness. | 'Rest is to go further' is an incomplete literal rendering.

text: Doing the work of a tea server, stove tender, and water carrier all at once - naturally, for only one salary.
note: was: Working as a tea worker, fire worker, and water carrier, of course only one salary. | Fixes the comma-spliced run-on; meaning (three jobs, one salary) preserved.

text: Hiding from prying eyes, secretly training in martial arts.
note: was: To cover up, they hid and secretly practiced martial arts. | Fixes the awkward dangling infinitive opener; 修練 rendered as 'training' to match the register.

text: You are the target of discrimination; even if you humbly seek guidance, no one pays attention, and instead you are mocked. All you can do is go off alone to find a quiet, secluded spot and train by yourself.
note: was: You are the target of discrimination; even if you humbly seek guidance, no one pays attention, and instead you are mocked. You can only be alone, seeking a quiet place to practice on your own. | Fixes the dangling 'You can only be alone, seeking...' construction; 'train' also aligns with the 修練 = Training fix on the paired title.

text: Practicing martial arts under your master's guidance.
note: was: Under the master's guidance, practice martial arts | Restores the missing final period and fixes the stray imperative fragment; 師父 = Master (one's own teacher) correctly kept.

text: The Qingcheng Skill-Transmission Elder guides disciples in martial arts here; you can seek guidance from nearby.
note: was: Qingcheng Master of Skill Transmission guides disciples in martial arts. You can seek guidance from the side. | NOMENCLATURE fixes 長老 as Elder, and explicitly disallows 'Master' outside 師父; 'Master of Skill Transmission' violated that.

text: Carrying medicinal pills, chopping knives, hoes, and other exclusive goods, they sell them on the way down the mountain while purchasing daily necessities and miscellaneous goods. It is time-consuming and often requires enduring the elements, facing wind and rain.
note: was: Carrying medicinal pills, chopping knives, hoes, and other exclusive goods, they sell them on the way down the mountain while purchasing daily necessities and miscellaneous goods. It is time‑consuming and often requires enduring the elements, facing wind and rain. | Strips the non-ASCII U+2011 hyphen.

text: (Unauthorized) serving as the guardian of the Junior Martial Sister, waiting under the window of the Women's Quarters from morning until night.
note: was: (Unauthorized) serving as the guardian of the Junior Martial Sister, waiting under the window of the female disciples' room from morning until night. | NOMENCLATURE/GLOSSARY: 女弟子房 = Women's Quarters.

text: The scenery is beautiful - the thirty-six peaks of Yin and Yang are each more stunning than the last - well worth a walk.
note: was: The scenery is beautiful, the thirty‑six peaks of Yin and Yang, no place is not extraordinary, you should go take a walk. | Fixes the non-ASCII hyphen and the four-clause comma splice.
was: Cultivation | GLOSSARY/NOMENCLATURE: 修練 is never Cultivation (reserved for 修養); 修練 = Training.
was: Cultivation | Same 修練 = Training fix as Position/title/training.
was: Cultivation | Same 修練 = Training fix.
